modules.title: Degree-Bounded Network Design: Balanced Tree Partitioning and DB-GST-T Rounding
modules.expensive_path: DBGSTSolver._solve_lp: builds and solves one scipy.optimize.linprog LP relaxation over all tree vertices (constraints (8)-(11) of Section 6), the one step whose cost scales with instance size rather than being O(n) combinatorial work.
modules.rationale: Single self-contained file implementing two results from one paper (Lemma 2.1 balanced tree partitioning; Theorem 1.2 DB-GST-T bicriteria rounding), sharing one module docstring, one license, one pin, no separate directories, no separate dependency sets, and no separate build. Part (A) is a thin combinatorial lemma (find one separator vertex, ~50 lines, no rich input/output contract of its own) that DB-GST-T's code does not call at runtime -- the two parts are demonstrated together in one __main__ block, not a pipeline stage. Neither part alone has enough independent scope to stand as its own repository-like module (SPEC.html's five-criteria test): whole-codebase default applies, same pattern as consistent-kmedian. Both parts are covered as separate checks of the same module at Step 3, not split into separate modules.
excluded: No separate unit tests exist to exclude; only the single demo example is available as official coverage.
hazards: No upstream repository or reference output: this is a self-authored, faithful simplification of the paper's algorithm, not a vendored third-party codebase.

Thin official-test surface: exactly one example script (the __main__ block) exercising each part once on one fixed random instance; no isolated unit tests of the LP construction, the power-of-2 rounding, the rescaling step, or the recursive randomized rounding individually.

DBGSTSolver.solve is randomized (self.rng = random.Random(seed), used in _recursive_round) and depends on scipy.optimize.linprog(method="highs") for the LP relaxation; both are deterministic given a fixed seed and fixed problem in the native run (verified byte-identical across two runs), but the LP method choice is a numerical dependency worth flagging for the pointwise-vs-invariants decision at STOP 4.

balanced_tree_partitioning's decomposition_depth rebuilds an induced sub-tree by iterating a Python set ("roots = [u for u in vertices if tree.parent.get(u) not in vertices]" then "sub.root = roots[0]") -- for this module's tree shape there is exactly one such root so the choice is not actually order-dependent, but a differently-shaped future input could make it so; worth a source-reading note at STOP 4/review.
modules.purpose: Single self-contained file implementing two results from one paper (Lemma 2.1 balanced tree partitioning; Theorem 1.2 DB-GST-T bicriteria rounding), sharing one module docstring, one license, one pin, no separate directories, no separate dependency sets, and no separate build. Part (A) is a thin combinatorial lemma that DB-GST-T's code does not call at runtime; the two parts are demonstrated together in one __main__ block, not a pipeline stage. Whole-codebase default applies, same pattern as consistent-kmedian.
primary_inputs: (A) BinaryTree: a rooted binary tree given as a root plus children/parent maps built via add_child
(B) DBGSTInstance: a rooted tree T-circ with per-vertex cost c_u, degree bound d_u, and k disjoint leaf groups O_1..O_k
primary_outputs: (A) balanced_tree_partition_vertex: one separator vertex v with n/3 < |descendants(v)| <= 2n/3+1; balanced_tree_partitioning: the (T1, T2) vertex-set split at v; decomposition_depth: the recursive decomposition height h
(B) DBGSTSolver.solve(): dict with V (chosen vertex set), cost, max_degree_violation_factor, groups_covered/groups_total, lp_value
algorithm_stages: (A) repeatedly descend to the heaviest child until the subtree size falls in (n/3, 2n/3+1] (balanced_tree_partition_vertex), then split the tree at that vertex (balanced_tree_partitioning), applied recursively (decomposition_depth)

(B) step 1: solve LP relaxation (7)-(12) via scipy.optimize.linprog(method="highs"); step 2: round the LP solution to non-positive powers of 2; step 3: rescale by a level-dependent factor with threshold gamma (Section 6.1); step 4: repeat recursive randomized rounding M times and union the results
unique_responsibilities: (A) produces the single balanced-separator primitive the paper's O(log n)-depth decomposition tree is built from
(B) produces a vertex set that (whp) connects every group while bounding cost to O(log n log k) times the LP optimum and degree violation to O(log n), per Theorem 1.2
not_responsible_for: No separate unit tests exist to exclude; only the single demo example is available as official coverage.

Theorem 1.1 (Degree-Bounded Directed Steiner Tree via state trees and a large LP over a super-tree T-circ) is explicitly not implemented by the source itself -- the module docstring states it is a quasi-polynomial-time construction not practical to reproduce as runnable code; there is nothing to package.
